enum HxDialogAttributes_t

Dialog attributes used by HxDialogSetAttributes.

Enumerator:
kHxDialogDefault 
kHxDialogAttrBlocking  If a dialog has the kHxDialogAttrBlocking attribute set, then the user cannot use the Apps key to switch applications until the dialog is closed. This attribute can be used by applications that need to complete an operation before being moved to the background. Use of this attribute is discouraged, since the user should be allowed to switch applications. If a blocking dialog is used, the blocking state begins only after the dialog is shown. The application should state in the dialog that that switching is disabled until the dialog is closed.

HxResult HxDialogCloseAllDialogs ( void   ) 

Close all open dialogs and alerts.

HxDialogCloseAllDialogs closes an application's open dialogs and alerts.

This function is intended to be called by applications when the application is being moved to the background (from its kHxApplicationIsDeactivated notification callback).

The system closes dialogs by sending a kHxCommandButtonChanged message for the dialog's command button tagged as the "escape" button with the HxDialogSetEscapeButton API, or with the "escape" resource attribute. If an escape button is not set by the application HX_MISSING_RESOURCE is returned and the function exits without closing more dialogs.

Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success.

HxResult HxDialogDelete ( HxDialog_t *  pDialog  ) 

Close a dialog.

HxDialogDelete is used to dismiss and deallocate a dialog created with HxDialogNew, HxColorDialogNew, or HxFileDialogNew.

This function is normally called from the dialog's command button callback in response to the user pressing the "OK" or "Cancel" command buttons.

Parameters:
pDialog IN: Pointer to dialog
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success.

HxResult HxDialogGetTitle ( HxDialog_t *  pDialog,
char **const   hText 
)

Get the title of the dialog.

HxDialogGetTitle returns a pointer the dialog's title.

The handle points to the pointer for the actual text of the dialog's title. The text should not be modified directly using the return value, since this would cause the field state to be in error. To change the title, use HxDialogSetTitle.

Parameters:
pDialog IN: Pointer to a dialog
hText OUT: Handle to the title string
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pDialog is NULL.

HxResult HxDialogNew ( uint32_t  id,
const HxRectangle_t *  pBounds,
const char *  pTitle,
HxDialog_t **  hDialog 
)

Create a dialog.

HxDialogNew is called to create and show a modal dialog window.

If pBounds is set to NULL, default values are used. Default values center the dialog in the display, and create a dialog that has a default width and height.

This function should be used for general purpose dialogs. For a color picker, use HxColorDialogNew. For File Open or File Save [As] dialogs, use HxFileDialogNew.

The toolkit returns an error is the application attempts to open a dialog with the same resource ID of a dialog that is already open. This check frees the application from performing the same check, provided the dialog is not created using the kHxWidgetAutoID constant when calling HxDialogNew (or using $AUTO in a dialog resource definition).

Parameters:
id IN: Dialog resource ID
pBounds IN: Rectangle describing the position and size of the dialog. If NULL, default values are used.
pTitle IN: Title of the dialog, or NULL
hDialog OUT: Handle to the created dialog
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success. *hDialog is set to NULL if there is an error.

HxResult HxDialogNewWithThemeButtons ( uint32_t  id,
const HxRectangle_t *  pBounds,
const char *  pTitle,
HxDialogThemeButtons_t  buttons,
HxDialogThemeButtonCallbackFnPtr  buttonCallback,
HxDialog_t **  hDialog 
)

Create a dialog with additional titlebar buttons.

HxDialogNew is called to create and show a modal dialog window.

This function should be used for applications that desire a close button in the top right corner of the dialog theme. It is a variation on the more standard HxDialogNew.

buttonCallback will be called when a button up occurs over a theme button.

Parameters:
id IN: Dialog resource ID
pBounds IN: Rectangle describing the position and size of the dialog. If NULL, default values are used.
pTitle IN: Title of the dialog, or NULL
buttons IN: Flags specifying which buttons to use in the titlebar.
buttonCallback IN: Callback for only theme button clicks.
hDialog OUT: Handle to the created dialog
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success. *hDialog is set to NULL if there is an error.

HxResult HxDialogSetEscapeButton ( HxDialog_t *  pDialog,
uint32_t  buttonID 
)

Set the "escape" command button.

HxDialogSetEscapeButton allows an application to indicate which command button should be acted on when the user presses the "escape" key. (The "escape" key is the top left key on the keyboard, the back-quote.) When the key is pressed, the system sends a kHxCommandButtonChanged message for the command button. Normally, this command button would be "Cancel", or its equivalent.

If the application disables this command button, then a message is not sent when the user presses the "escape" key.

If the dialog has an editable field, and if the field has focus, then the key is sent to the field rather than to the command button.

Parameters:
pDialog IN: Pointer to a dialog
buttonID IN: Resource ID of the command button
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NULL_POINTER if pDialog is NULL. Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if the button ID is not associated with a command button in the dialog.

HxResult HxDialogShowAndWait ( HxDialog_t *  pDialog  ) 

Show or hide a dialog.

This function is used to show a dialog. It is a synchronous variation of HxDialog(pDialog, true).

This function returns after the application's call to HxDialogDelete.

pDialog IN: Pointer to a dialog
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success.
